**Average / Median House Price – California (latest publicly‑available figures)**  

| Metric | Approximate Value | Notes |
|--------|-------------------|-------|
| **Median sales price (Q 1 2024)** | **$860 000–$880 000** | Based on Zillow’s “California Housing Market” report & Redfin data. Median means half of all homes sold above this amount and half below it. |
| **Mean (average) sales price (2023‑24)** | **≈ $940 000–$960 000** | Mean tends to be higher than the median because a handful of very expensive properties pull the arithmetic average upward. |
| **National comparison** | National median ≈ $400 000 | California remains roughly double the U.S. median. |

### Key Takeaways

* **Regional Variation:**  
  * Coastal metros such as San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Orange County, and Santa Clara consistently see median prices well over \$1 million.  
  * Inland regions—e.g., Fresno, Bakersfield, Modesto—have medians closer to \$350 k–\$450 k.  
  * Even within a single county, neighborhoods can differ dramatically (e.g., Palo Alto > \$5M vs. East Oakland < \$300k).

* **Trends Over Time:**  
  * From 2019 through early 2024, California’s median home price has risen at an annual rate of roughly **8%–10%**, outpacing many other states.  
  * Interest rates, supply constraints, and migration patterns continue to drive demand, especially in tech hubs.

* **Sources (most recent):**  
  * [Zillow Research – California](https://www.zillow.com/research/california/) – provides quarterly median sale prices and HVI trends.  
  * [Redfin Data Center – California](https://www.redfin.com/states/us/california/housing-data) – offers monthly median sale prices and inventory levels.  
  * [U.S. Census Bureau – American Community Survey (ACS)](https://data.census.gov/cedsci/table?q=household+income&tid=ACSDT5Y2020.B19013) – gives broader socioeconomic context.

---

#### Quick Reference Numbers (rounded)

| Category | Typical Range |
|----------|---------------|
| **High‑end markets** (San Fran, SF Bay, Silicon Valley) | \$1.2 m – \$3 m+ |
| **Mid‑range suburban** (Los Angeles suburbs, Riverside, Sacramento) | \$500 k – \$750 k |
| **Inland/rural** (Fresno, Bakersfield, Stockton) | \$250 k – \$400 k |

> **Bottom line:** If you’re looking at the overall state picture, expect a median resale price near **\$870 k** and an average (mean) price close to **\$950 k** as of early 2024. These figures will shift slightly each quarter depending on market dynamics, so always check the latest local listings or real‑estate analytics dashboards before making decisions.
